name: histogram
purpose: Accessible SVG histogram of the distribution of raw numeric values in adjacent bins on a linear axis: automatic bins (Sturges' rule on nice boundaries), a bin count, or explicit thresholds. Every bin is a keyboard-reachable bar ("10 to 20: 14 values"), with tooltips, a generated summary naming the most frequent bin and out-of-range values, and a data table fallback. The binning is exported as computeBins.
whenToUse: The shape of a distribution of one numeric variable (response times, amounts, scores).
Checking skew, spread, and outliers before choosing a summary statistic.
whenNotToUse: Comparing distributions of several groups: use Box Plot.
Relationships between two variables: use Scatter Chart.
responsive: Width follows the container (ResizeObserver); height is the height option. Bin edge labels are thinned so they never crowd. Reflows at 320 CSS px.
rtl: direction rtl mirrors the x axis (lowest bin at the right), puts the count axis on the right, and swaps ArrowLeft/ArrowRight. Tooltip and table follow the document direction.
theme: Colors from color-chart-1..8 by palette slot; gridlines color-chart-grid; axes color-chart-axis; text color-text / color-text-muted; tooltip color-surface with color-border-strong. Forced colors use CanvasText, Canvas, GrayText, and Highlight.
timezone: Not applicable: numeric axes only; no dates are formatted.
security: All text (title, description, labels, values, tooltip, table) is set with textContent; SVG is built with createElementNS. Colors are CSS classes; sizes and the tooltip position are written through the CSSOM (style.setProperty). No innerHTML, no style attributes, no inline handlers: works under style-src without unsafe-inline and require-trusted-types-for.
dataHandling: Renders the data it is given; no persistence, network access, or telemetry. Values are not logged; validation errors name the option, never its value.

budgets.metric: Histogram.create, 10,000 values, including binning and the first render
budgets.budget: < 40 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

performance.testedScale: Measured in tests/e2e/perf-r3.spec.ts with 10,000 values. Binning is one pass for the extent plus a binary search per value; the DOM has one node per bin (Sturges asks for 15 bins at 10,000 values; a bin count of up to 500 gives about that many). The data table is built only when opened (toggle mode).

limitations: One data set per chart (no overlaid distributions).
Bins are lower-inclusive; the last bin is also upper-inclusive.
Only integer count ticks are printed.
unsupported: Density curves, cumulative histograms, and logarithmic axes.
HTML content in labels or tooltips.
antiPatterns: Too many bins for the data size (sparse, noisy bars).
Comparing groups by overlaying several histograms (use Box Plot).
